html:
SMTO-FIL-0015 — SMTO wasn't sure which part of the file to change

GUID: 6b7d86e6-6fab-421f-8fda-df73da2ec54e
Slug: file-match-not-unique
Domain: FIL · Subsystem: files

What happened

  • The text SMTO wanted to replace appears a different number of times than it planned, usually more than once, so it couldn't tell which place to change. The file wasn't changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If only one place should change, tell SMTO which one, for example "the line under Contact details", and ask it to try again. Naming the spot lets SMTO include nearby words so it matches only that place.
  2. If every place with that text should change, tell SMTO to change all of them. SMTO then plans for the real number of matches instead of just one.
  3. If anyone else has edited the file, ask SMTO to read it again before trying. Edits made elsewhere can add or remove copies of the same text.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reports the edit as done and only the places you meant show the new text.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't ask SMTO to resend the same edit unchanged; it will stop again for the same reason.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Gateway file.edit was rejected because an edit's old_text occurs a number of times (actual_occurrences) different from expected_occurrences, which defaults to 1; nothing was written.

What this means

  • The number of old_text occurrences differs from expected_occurrences, whose default is one. File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.

Why this can happen

  • The number of old_text occurrences differs from expected_occurrences, whose default is one.

How to diagnose it

  • Count the actual matches and distinguish zero, too few and too many; this guard is not limited to multiple matches.

How to fix it

  • Compare actual_occurrences in the receipt with the current file. Either extend old_text with surrounding context until it is unique, or set expected_occurrences to the deliberately intended count, then retry against the current expected_revision (gateway_core/file_mutate.edit).
  • Read the current matches and deliberately correct the context or expected count before editing.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The reviewed edit matches exactly the intended expected count.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.
